# ATLAS Explain

> Market jargon explained in plain language, inside your AI assistant. A free, read-only MCP connector (no account, no key) with official figures, crypto prices and charts, economic data and headlines, each with its source and time. Education only: it never recommends a trade or forecasts a price.

Connector address (Streamable HTTP, no auth): https://atlas-explain-mcp.atlas-explain.workers.dev/mcp
MCP Registry name: io.github.MISHHF93/atlas-explain

## Start here

- [Add it to your assistant](https://atlas-explain.web.app/connect): steps for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code, plus every tool and prompt
- [Support and FAQ](https://atlas-explain.web.app/support)
- [How it's built](https://atlas-explain.web.app/how-its-built): sources, refresh times and what is never collected

## Tools

- explain_term, browse_glossary: market terms in plain language, and a learning path
- asset_details, evidence_brief: one asset with every fact sourced, plus what the facts don't tell you
- official_figures: US Treasury yields, ECB and Bank of Canada rates, EIA energy prices, SEC-filed company figures
- crypto_prices, price_history, market_depth: ten major coins, charts over 24 hours to 30 days, spreads and order-book depth
- economy_snapshot, economic_calendar: inflation, jobs, policy rates, US debt, and the next central-bank rate decisions
- money_maths: compound growth, fees, inflation and diversification from the person's own numbers, as a chart they can change
- scam_red_flags: warning signs of investment fraud in a message or offer, where to check registration and where to report
- treasury_auctions: upcoming US Treasury auctions and the latest results
- compare_countries: GDP growth, inflation, unemployment and GDP per person across the G20, from the World Bank
- data_series: dated rows and CSV of official economic series, with source and licence, for charts, spreadsheets and reports
- rate_change_impact: what a rate change would do to your own mortgage payment, HELOC, savings or GIC/CD, to the cent; never a forecast
- decision_explainer: the Fed's, Bank of Canada's, ECB's or Bank of England's latest rate decision from its own statement, how the wording changed, and what it says it is weighing
- speech_tracker: recent speeches by Fed, Bank of Canada, ECB and Bank of England policymakers, with the bank's own description and a link
- notable_today: what stands out in the data today, each item with the rule that picked it
- todays_headlines: official press releases and recent market news
